linkedin.headline: Creator and CEO of Eve by Boz, Hall of Fame Inducted Marketing Executive, & Author of “The Urgent Life”, Curator of The Badass Workshop
linkedin.summary:
Bozoma Saint John is the Creator and CEO of Eve by Boz, a Hall of Fame inducted Marketing Executive, author of The Urgent Life, and general badass.

She created Eve by Boz, which is a hair and hair care company that is redefining the industry with a unique approach that blends cultural authenticity and premium quality. The brand is committed to empowering Black women and women of color by offering hair extensions that not only look stunning but celebrate their natural beauty and are created in Ghana. The accompanying hair care line is formulated with indigenous ingredients from Africa like baobab tree oil, moringa, rosehip, shea butter and palm kernel oil. Eve by Boz is not just a brand; it’s a movement that celebrates the beauty, resilience, and diversity of Black women and women of color.  

Boz got her start in marketing at Spike Lee’s agency, SpikeDDB. She then went on to manage brands at PepsiCo, before becoming Head of Music and Entertainment Marketing. After that, she led Global Consumer Marketing at Apple Music & iTunes; before serving as Chief Brand Officer at Uber; she then took on the CMO role for Endeavor; after which she served as the Global CMO at Netflix. Bozoma left her corporate track to publish her memoir, The Urgent Life and has taken her personality to The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills. 

Bozoma has been inducted into the American Marketing Association Hall of Fame and the American Advertising Federation Hall of Achievement. Forbes named her the #1 Most Influential CMO. She was inducted into Billboard's Women in Music Hall of Fame and honored as Executive of the Year. She has graced the cover of Adweek and has also been featured on various prestigious lists, including The Hollywood Reporter’s Women in Entertainment Power 100 and Fast Company’s and Ad Age’s Most Creative People.

In 2021, Harvard Business School published a multi-media case study on her career, titled “Leading with Authenticity and Urgency”; through which she developed and taught a program at the University named “The Anatomy of a Badass.” Boz has also created a class, “The Badass Workshop” to teach the nuances of achieving success and building your life on your own terms.

Boz has been named as an Ambassador for the African Diaspora and Special Envoy to the President of Ghana. She is also a philanthropic Ambassador to Pencils of Promise in Ghana and serves on the boards of Vital Voices, Soho House, the Black Advisory Board for the CFDA and Wesleyan University.

All of that said, she counts her highest achievement as being a mother to her 15-year-old daughter, Lael.

positions.title: Creator and CEO
positions.description:
Eve by Boz has been created to revolutionize the hair extensions industry with a unique approach that blends cultural authenticity and premium quality. The brand aims to make a difference in a sector that acutely affects Black women and women of color but has long overlooked our needs. While some might see it as superficial, it is serious for those of us who spend our hard earned money and received so little in return. Despite Black women and women of color making up 80% of the buying power, we have no say in how these products are constructed and we spend an inordinate amount of time customizing products that should be made with us in mind in the first place.
The brand is committed to empowering Black women and women of color by offering wigs, bundles, and closures which are sourced from Asia, created in Ghana, and distributed globally. Additionally, the specially formulated hair care products harness the power of indigenous ingredients like baobab oil, moringa, shea butter, palm kernel oil, and rosehip. Infused into every strand of hair, these natural oils transform raw extensions into luxurious, manageable, and long-lasting products. Adding to the sensory experience, the hair care line has captivating fragrances that keep hair smelling fresh for weeks giving them a richness that reflects our origins.
Eve by Boz is not just a brand; it’s a movement that celebrates the beauty, resilience, and diversity of Black women and women of color worldwide.

positions.title: Author of The Urgent Life
positions.description: When my husband, Peter Saint John, died of cancer, I made one big decision: to live life with urgency. I’m no stranger to adversity, having lost my college boyfriend to suicide, navigated an interracial marriage, grieved a child born prematurely–a process that led to me and Peter’s separation–and navigated coparenting the daughter who me and Peter shared. When Peter knew his cancer was terminal, he gave me a short list of things to do: cancel the divorce, and fix the wrongs immediately. In THE URGENT LIFE, I take readers through the dizzying, numbing days of grief, and the courage which it sparked in my to live life in accordance with my deepest values time and time again. You’ll witness my journey forward through multiple griefs, as I navigate life as a single parent and build a truly remarkable career. My story is extraordinary, but my grief is not uncommon, and my courage is sure to touch any reader who has loved, mourned and found a path through loss and grief, as well as anyone who’s struggled to live life to its fullest.

Ketanji Brown Jackson is a living testimony and a charge for us to PERSEVERE!!!

When she shared this story during her confirmation, it hit me in my core. To be completely transparent, I didn’t watch much of the hearings because I was so triggered by watching this accomplished, incredibly well (and over) qualified Black woman being subjected to condescending and ridiculing questioning. It felt too close, too familiar, too much. She told of being in spaces in which she wasn’t supposed to belong, and feeling homesick for comfort. So when she told this story a few weeks ago, I was (and still am) questioning myself a lot about the toll it takes to constantly be in that space. I’ve asked myself why continue, why persist, why push when I can simply lay down my sword. 

But I don’t succumb. And I won’t. And neither does she. And today Ketanji Brown Jackson has made history! So I’m celebrating her… and all of us who PRESERVE despite our circumstances, despite the ceilings, despite the homesickness for comfort… ONWARD!!!!

#SupremeCourtJustice
#CallHerByHerName
#AndPronounceItRightToo

Thank you @carichampion for sending this to me at a moment when I needed it most. I love you.

“IF I’M NOT VISIBLE, IF I’M NOT TELLING MY OWN STORY, THEN NO ONE WILL KNOW.  They won’t know the pain of it. They won’t know the joy of it.  They won’t know the struggle of it. They won’t know the triumph of it. They won’t know the success of it. They won’t know the badassness of it. SO I HAVE TO TELL IT.” 

🗣🎤

You’ve all shown us so much love this week 🥰❤️ so come a little closer… if you’ve never experienced a traditional Ghanaian marriage, let me take you inside ours.

We originally made this @mintedweddings program for our wedding guests who traveled to Ghana from the US and UK, many of whom had never experienced a traditional Ghanaian marriage.

Now that the whole internet seems to have joined the wedding 😅, I realize some of y’all need the program too.

It mattered deeply to us that our marriage ceremony be deeply and intentionally Ghanaian; staying true to the traditions that have been carried for millennia.

The knocking. The gifts. The negotiations. The groom’s family coming to ask for the “flower” in the house. The families agreeing. And finally, the bride being brought before them to answer the only question that really matters:

Should we accept this family’s offer?

Well… you know what I said. YES!!!! 

AKWAABA. Let me show you how we marry.

#BozAndKeely

ESSENCE Exclusive: For Bozoma Saint John-Watson, her wedding was more than a celebration of love—it was a vivid expression of the Ghanaian heritage, cultural pride and bold personal style that shape her values.

The TV personality married her longtime love, Keely Watson, in front of 1,000 friends and family during their Ghanaian wedding ceremony in Accra, Ghana. Their Ghanaian regalia was a focal point. This was by design.

Saint John-Watson wanted to use her big day to showcase Ghanaian culture and fashion, two things dear to her heart. From authentic kente woven in Bonwire and layers of gold to traditional Ahenema royal leather slippers, every detail was intentional.

And the fashion didn’t stop there. Her reception looks included a kente and beaded masterpiece by Accra-based designer Mimmy Yeboah, custom kente Christian Louboutin heels and a multi-colored hand-beaded mini dress by Kenneth Tetteh.

For Saint John-Watson, the celebration was also about expanding how Black people see beauty, tradition and bridal fashion.

Visit ESSENCE.com to read more about the details of their beautiful wedding.

Photos: @focusandblur

WAIT. WE’VE BEEN MARRIED A WHOLE MONTH?!?!! RUN IT BACK. 🥹😅🥰

One month ago, our love had a soundtrack. It wore kente and gold. It danced. It laughed. It crossed oceans. It gathered the people we love in Ghana and gave us a day we still can’t believe was ours.

We’re not over how spectacular it was. We’re not sure we ever will be. And honestly, we don’t want to be.

To every person who put their hands, hearts and genius into making this day what it was: THANK YOU. We hope you can see yourselves in every beautiful frame.

One month down. And two months to go until our American wedding when we get to do this again!!!

Beverly Hills… let’s gooooo!!!! 

#WeddingSeason
#GhanaianWedding
#Newlywed

NADIA. @queennad_5b by handle, QUEEN by every definition.

I met her during the Year of Return, when we were working together to call the diaspora home to Ghana. I couldn’t have known then that somewhere between the work, the dreaming, the strategizing, the building and all the life that happened in between, she would become my bestie in Ghana. My sister. My constant.

And maybe there’s something beautifully full-circle about the fact that years later, when @keelywatson and I decided to have our Ghanaian wedding, Nadia was right beside us to plan it. This enormous undertaking of family, tradition, culture, people and production was in her hands. Because in so many ways, we were still doing the work. Only this time, it was deeply personal. What began years ago as an invitation for the diaspora to come home became my own family’s celebration of love, tradition and belonging… and that celebration traveled around the world, putting Ghanaian culture on screens and in conversations we could never have imagined when we first started working together.

And my girl had her hands AND her heart all over it.

That’s Nadia. She shows up. For her country. For her people. For her friends. And most especially for the FIVE young men lucky enough to call her Mom, and the very fortunate man who calls her Wife.

So on your 50th, my prayer is BIG because you have loved us BIG. May God astonish you with what He does with the next 50 years. May He return every ounce of love you’ve poured into the rest of us, multiplied beyond anything you could ask or imagine. May His favor chase you down. And may you stand in absolute AWE of His goodness.

Happy 50th birthday, QUEEN NAD. I love you beyond words.
